event.name: YCNCC Visiting Scholar Panel: The Rise of Climate Engineering
event.descriptionText: Can we engineer our way out of climate change? Engineering approaches to averting the worst impacts of climate change, from carbon dioxide removal to solar radiation management, are drawing growing attention. This panel discussion will delve into questions surrounding who decides which planet-cooling technologies get funded, tested and deployed; how we balance geopolitical risks, economic trade-offs and geochemical realities; and the role universities should play in shaping a safe and equitable climate agenda. Panelists David Keith (University of Chicago, YCNCC Fall 2026 Visiting Scholar), Ken Gillingham (Yale School of the Environment), Noah Planavsky (Yale Earth & Planetary Sciences), and Jessica Seddon (Jackson School of Global Affairs) bring perspectives from climate science, economics, and geochemistry. YCNCC Faculty and Associate Professor of Chemical & Environmental Engineering David Kwabi) will moderate.
